_why: alpha-engine-config-I8981. Every `paused` trigger in automation_pause.json names the OPEN tracker issue that owns switching it back on, the date past which the pause is no longer justified by anything, and the condition that releases it - the trigger-side mirror of `paused_alarms`' `issue`/`re_exam` (alpha-engine-config-I8047). Measured 2026-10-27: 22 of the 39 paused triggers carried a machine-readable owner (a `Pause-owner:` line on alpha-engine-config-I6984) and 13 named no open issue at all; the 2026-08-07 ruling's own issue, I6617, closed the day it was filed. Keys are `<surface>:<name>`, the grammar of the `Pause-owner:` line and of _freshness_monitor/disabled_producers.json. Kept in its own file, not in automation_pause.json, because several deploy workflows (data-collection stack, crypto-balances, overseer-backstop-responder) run on any edit to that file and a release declaration changes no live state. automation_pause.py `release_findings()` asserts every paused trigger has a well-formed entry here and that no entry outlives its trigger; it does NOT resolve the issue's state or compare the date to today - that needs a tracker credential this repo does not hold, and is graded in alpha-engine-config. Never edit an entry to re-enable a trigger: re-enabling is Brian's ruling (principles.md 2.5).
